text:
Tampa Bay arrives off a 4-2 win over Vancouver in which the Lightning came back from two goals down, the Canucks' seventh straight game without a win. TBL is 4-1-0 in its last five. Vegas has won three straight, including a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh, and is playing without Parker Wotherspoon. The story here is a Lightning team whose record undersells its play against a Golden Knights team whose results have run ahead of theirs.

Tampa Bay has taken 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, to 53% for Vegas. Vegas's goal difference of +17 comes on +8.4 expected, with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. TBL's +4 sits on +9.2 expected, so its finishing has cost it. The Golden Knights have the better special teams numbers: 0.89 expected power-play goals per game and 0.30 allowed on the penalty kill, against 0.66 and 0.53 for the Lightning. The model has it close, at 3.08 goals for TBL and 2.90 for VGK.

In net, projected starter Andrei Vasilevskiy has been below expectation this season (-0.25 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what the shots should allow) after a strong +23.15 last year. Carter Hart is at +1.98 this year after -4.44 last year. For TBL, watch Brandon Hagel (43% to score) and Nikita Kucherov (37% to score, 82% to get a point). For VGK, Brett Howden plays his 500th game on a four-game point streak, and Mitch Marner has a six-game point streak.
